title: Time–Memory Trade-offs in MiMC Interpolation and GCD Attacks
summary: For MiMC-129/129 with an attacker-memory budget of two raised to the sixty-fourth power bytes, 38 rounds suffice against the named attacks; time–memory trade-offs remain open.

formal_statement.body: For $\mathrm{MiMC}$, characterize possible time--memory trade-offs for interpolation and GCD attacks when the attacker cannot store all required polynomial coefficients. Determine whether additional computation can compensate for limited storage and quantify the resulting attack complexity. A concrete baseline is $\mathrm{MiMC}\text{-}129/129$: with attacker memory limited to $2^{64}$ bytes, 38 rounds suffice against interpolation, GCD, and other attacks, while possible time--memory trade-offs remain unresolved.

scope.domain: Algebraic cryptanalysis of MiMC through interpolation and GCD attacks, with MiMC-129/129 as the concrete baseline.
assumptions: The attacker cannot store all required polynomial coefficients.
parameters: Attacker memory: limits coefficient storage, with 2^64 bytes in the concrete MiMC-129/129 baseline
Round count: 38 rounds suffice in that baseline against interpolation, GCD, and other attacks
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether additional computation can compensate for limited coefficient storage and quantify the resulting time–memory trade-offs and attack complexity for interpolation and GCD attacks.

citations.label: MiMC: Efficient Encryption and Cryptographic Hashing with Minimal Multiplicative Complexity

progress.summary: The paper states that 38 rounds protect MiMC-129/129 against interpolation, GCD, and other attacks when attacker memory is capped at 2^64 bytes, then explicitly leaves possible time–memory trade-offs for future research.
